prompts.business: Use TradeFlow MCP connection {{serverName}}. Its available tools are: {{tools}}. Query tools are read-only. Use staging tools only when I explicitly ask to record inbound or outbound transactions. Draft submissions remain pending human review and do not create formal records or change inventory; never describe them as completed transactions. First list available tools and run a minimal inventory query with {"page":1,"limit":5}. When a result has more pages, paginate with limit no greater than 100. For the requested date range, report the currency and FIFO costing basis returned by the tools. Then summarize this month’s sales, cost and profit by customer. If financial tools are unavailable, explain the account’s permissions instead of inventing numbers.
prompts.repair:
Help diagnose my TradeFlow MCP connection in {{client}}. Server: {{server}}. Profile: {{profile}}. Managed server name: {{serverName}}. User configuration path: {{configPath}}.

The GUI signs in to my TradeFlow account, creates an independent 90-day MCP credential, stores it locally with user-only permissions, and installs this managed connection. Remote mode uses {{server}}/mcp with a Bearer header. OpenCode V2 uses mcp.servers with type remote and oauth false; WorkBuddy uses mcpServers with type streamableHttp, url and headers. Bridge mode starts the bundled helper with serve --profile {{profile}}. Query tools are read-only. When staging writes are enabled, editor and superuser connections can submit transaction drafts for human review; only the web app can merge them. Reader connections remain read-only.

1. Run the diagnostic and read only its redacted JSON:
{{doctor}}
2. If the configuration is missing or damaged, repair it:
{{repair}}
3. Run diagnostics again and verify configurationWritten and serviceVerified. These do not prove host activation. Enable/trust or reload the host, list TradeFlow tools and make one minimal query. Use draft tools only when I explicitly request transaction recording; every draft still needs human review.
4. If the host cannot use remote Streamable HTTP while the endpoint passes diagnostics, use the bundled bridge:
{{bridge}}
5. HTTP 401 or expired/revoked credentials require me to sign in to the GUI and update the connection. HTTP 403 requires checking the account permissions. HTTP 404 requires checking the backend MCP setting and reverse proxy. HTTP 429 requires waiting. Network/TLS errors require restoring connectivity; never bypass certificate validation. Explain project overrides without silently changing project files.

Do not open credential files, print full MCP configurations, place tokens in chat, or change account permissions or host security settings. Show the redacted diagnosis, actions taken and whether a real host query succeeded. State explicitly when I must trust or reload the host.
